reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes DFT-based transport calculations and ML force fields for thermal conductivity in other materials, but provides no specific support for the key premises about HfNbTaTiZr, the predicted equal contributions at low T, the 30% suppression, or the factor-of-2 error reduction.
premises: ML model trained on DFT data can separately predict lattice and electronic thermal conductivity
At low T (<200 K), lattice and electronic contributions are nearly equal
At high T (300-1200 K), lattice contribution is ~30% lower than Debye-based predictions
Overall prediction error is reduced by a factor of ~2 relative to earlier analytical models
DFT training data can capture configurational disorder and oxygen doping effects
